newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to firm on continued tankan euphoria.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to firm on continued tankan euphoria.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to firm on Thursday amid a continued euphoric mood over the economy created by the Bank of Japan's surprisingly positive "tankan" survey released on Wednesday, brokers said.
But they said that despite the optimism, gains were likely to be limited as there were few other factors to keep investors buying.
Profit-taking could also emerge, they said.
On Wednesday, the 225-share Nikkei average jumped 337.34 points or 1.66 percent to close at 20,679.27. Its September futures added 390 points to finish at 20,760.

"There is still some more room for short-covering in banking shares, and with turnover rising gradually there is a chance that brokerages, which have faced heavy selling recently, could rebound and support the Nikkei average," said Mitsuru Hayashino, Sanyo Securities general manager.
On Wednesday turnover swelled to 512 million shares from 366 million shares on the previous day.

"The near-term goal for the Nikkei is 20,800 as there are not enough factors apart from a good supply-demand situation to keep the index rising to 21,000 and beyond," a general manager at a foreign brokerage said.
"Stocks rose across the board on Wednesday due to the signs of brightness in the economy, but today trade should be more focused," he added.
